newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bonds seen consolidative pre-payrolls.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds seen consolidative pre-payrolls.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures, which have made handsome gains so far this week, are likely to be more consolidative ahead of the April U.S. employement report due out Friday, market analysts said.
Although mid- to longer-term views were divided on whether the market had already bottomed out, analysts generally agreed bonds looked toppish in the near term.
"In front of the employment report tomorrow, I don't really expect it to make any significant headway to the upside," said Mathew Crosson, director of fixed income at Pegasus Econometrics Group.
He said the June T-bond contract would probably struggle getting past the 110-area, a historical resistance level.
Still, Crosson was in the relatively bullish camp and noted that the market this week had broken out of a month-long basing pattern and price actions were generally constructive.
After Tuesday's two-point rally, bonds on Wednesday briefly dipped toward the top of the basing-pattern range and bounced higher, he noted.
In that process, the June contract broke above 109-6/32, the 38.2-percent retracement of the February-April decline, and that level has now become good support, he added.
June T-bonds dipped in early trade to 109-6/32 but edged up to the mid-109 area by late morning, up about a quarter point on the day.
Crosson said he would buy dips toward support at 108-25/32.
On the other hand, Stewart Taylor, president of Taylor Consulting, said the market was still in a bear trend overall and he would be looking for opportunities to establish short positions.

"I think we've been in a corrective (upward) phase," Taylor said. "The 110-area is very, very strong resistance, and I'm planning over the next few days to replace some of the shorts that I took off (squared) a couple of weeks ago."
He added that there were various resistance levels in the 110-1/32 to 110-16/32 zone.
He said today's 109-6/32 was immediate support and the next target would be the 108-12/32 to 108-15/32 area, the top of the mid-April ranges.
